messages.subject: convergence in inla
parts:
I’m working on the simulation results and I would like to know the convergence of the inla model. For example, if I want to obtain the converge in the glm case with R, I can extract:

model1<-glm(................family=" ",data=)

model1$converged

[1] TRUE

I don’t know if exist a similar function in the inla package.

Thanks in advance,

Martí Casals

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] convergence in inla
parts:
On Tue, 2012-10-23 at 05:41 -0700, Martí Casals wrote:
>
> I’m working on the simulation results and I would like to know the
> convergence of the inla model. For example, if I want to obtain the
> converge in the glm case with R, I can extract:
> model1<-glm(................family=" ",data=)
>
>
> model1$converged
>
> [1] TRUE
>
> I don’t know if exist a similar function in the inla package.

Although its not the same, you can check if this one is 0:


> y=1
> r=inla(y~1, data = data.frame(y))
> r$mode$mode.status
[1] 0


as INLA use *many* optimizations, not just one as for glm, then you
cannot compare really. anyhow, if everything is fine, then r$mode
$mode.status is 0. increasing value means that more is 'not fine', but
likely, the results are still useful.

H
